---
title: "017 — Mock-LLM chat test suite"
---

> **Status:** standing (extended, not superseded, by
> [020 — RC UI verification](020-rc-ui-verification.qmd))

**Goal.** Automated Playwright E2E coverage of the full chat experience —
onboarding, send/receive, rendering — with no live LLM, no API key, no external
network, and zero changes to the product codebase. The work began as idea
004-automated-chat-testing, whose decisions.md verdict picked the contrarian
stock-mock-server card over building a mock provider into the product — the
owner's reasoning: "the most complete and does the job well."

**Why.** Every E2E test that traversed a chat reply needed a live provider, so
request-path tests got skipped or flaked, and rendering assertions were too
nondeterministic to automate without fixed content. The card table had already
priced the rejected alternative precisely: a sixth, mock provider kind would
thread through the closed factory switch and every per-kind dialect table
forever, skip the key-storage path by construction (keyless), and bypass the
server proxy — the exact paths the suite exists to witness.

**Outcome & reversals.** The stand-in is a ~100-line dependency-free Node
fixture speaking the OpenAI chat protocol, because protocol fidelity was the
acceptance bar and the app's expectations were unusually specific: a terminal
`finish_reason` chunk is mandatory, SSE and single-shot JSON share one endpoint,
and a fresh chat's first turn fires three concurrent calls (reply, title,
brief) that all need answers. A `mock-llm` compose service is reachable only
inside the docker network — the server container's proxy is where provider
fetches execute — and the suite onboards it through the real settings UI via
the LiteLLM template, saving a placeholder key through the real IndexedDB path.
One deterministic kitchen-sink markdown document, with known structure and
known offsets, drives assertions over markdown structure, KaTeX math, mermaid,
copy affordances, and expound source alignment. Two product bugs blocked the
round trip and were fixed as documented exceptions to the zero-diff rule, each
with its regression test per the constitution: a cold direct load of `/chat`
rendered a 500, and the draft restore clobbered a prompt typed while the chat
was still loading. A known sourcemap edge — multi-line display math
desynchronizing alignment — was deliberately recorded as a follow-up, the
fixture avoiding it. Landed across PRs #17 and #21 (2026-09-02/03), shipped in
0.6.0 with the new CI e2e job validated green at 2m52s; the suite later
survived the auth gate landing by learning to wait out the security-setup
prompt.

**Learnings.**

- Test scaffolding owned by tests stays protocol-exact; a product mock kind
  inherits every provider-seam refactor forever and never exercises the real
  paths.
- A mock that answers in the wrong shape produces confidence that is false, not
  merely reduced — fidelity is the whole game.
- The first green round trip through the real UI is a bug detector: it surfaced
  two product defects no unit suite had caught.
- Name a zero-diff constraint's exception process up front, so real bugs get
  fixed with regression tests instead of breaking the guarantee quietly.
- Write the no-interception guardrail ("everything through the real proxy hop")
  down before the first flake, not after.
